summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of pancreatitis was admitted for severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. He had recently resumed heavy alcohol use. His presentation and elevated lipase were consistent with acute pancreatitis, and he was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control. He exhibited signs of alcohol withdrawal, including tremors, and was treated with CIWA protocol without complications. Imaging revealed cirrhosis with portal hypertension and an exophytic liver mass; MRI suggested the mass was a cirrhotic or dysplastic nodule, not hepatocellular carcinoma. His pain improved, diet was advanced, and he remained stable. He was discharged home with a short supply of oxycodone, continued liver and asthma medications, and referrals for alcohol abstinence counseling and specialist follow-up.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
